capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Hyundai release: Long Range models 77.4 to 84 kWh; XRT linked to the 84 kWh battery; bare capacity recorded as gross.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: European listing of the same 84 kWh pack (MY24): 80.0 kWh usable. Pack is shared across markets.

chemistry.notes: EV Database: NMC cathode, pouch (84 kWh pack); SK On NCM 811 per WeeklyDriver (already on file for 2026).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 697 V nominal, 800 V architecture.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: the US 2025 owner's manual page (code NE1a) describes manual plus navigation-automatic Battery Conditioning; the page does not name the model, NE1 being the IONIQ 5 platform code (inference). Same wording on the 2026 page.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: US 2026 IONIQ 5 page states 10.9 kW home charging for the 84 kWh car (already on file for 2026); 2025 is the same generation and onboard charger. Source is a US page; no Canadian page states the onboard charger, so Canadian cars on this powertrain (2025-2026) rely on the same carry-over.

dc_max_kw.notes: US 2025 first drive relays a "peak rate of 257 kW" on a 350 kW CCS charger (Hyundai US figure; Wikipedia infobox also 257). Conflicts: EV Database 263 kW (Hyundai Europe claims 260 kW), Wikipedia spec table 238 kW, Car and Driver measured about 258 kW.
